summary: Repaired node1’s FIFO consumer. It now accepts successive producers, appends only complete nonempty lines, blocks without busy-looping while disconnected, exits cleanly on SIGTERM, and starts automatically after reboot. Existing records, RHEL 10.0, and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 were preserved.
actions_performed: Replaced consumer.py with a Python 3-compatible blocking reconnect loop.
Added and enabled fifo-worker-consumer.service with filesystem hardening and SIGTERM shutdown.
Preserved the original script as /root/consumer.py.pre-reconnection-repair with mode 0600.
Tested separate producer connections, LF/CRLF blank lines, an incomplete line, idle CPU usage, and SIGTERM exit status.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified the changed boot identity, recovered service, retained data, and post-reboot FIFO processing.

evidence.requirement: Successive producers work without restarting the consumer
evidence.summary: Two independent producer connections were processed by unchanged PID 2070 with zero service restarts.

evidence.requirement: Retain previous records and record only complete nonempty lines
evidence.summary: previous-job remained present; valid jobs were appended; blank and unterminated records were absent.

evidence.requirement: Avoid a busy loop with no producer connected
evidence.summary: The idle consumer remained sleeping and accumulated zero CPU ticks before and after reboot.
systemd stopped the consumer with Result=success and exit status 0, then started it successfully under a new PID.

evidence.requirement: Preserve installed OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: The node remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64.

Healthy baseline boot ID 646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28 was captured; reboot was acknowledged; node1 returned with boot ID 5a2851d5-4117-4979-8866-a744ceb8b4af; the enabled service recovered with retained records and accepted a new post-reboot job.
